about: A strict ranking of the top n units by posterior mean: M (pairCount), the expected number of wrong directions of the posterior-mean order and, with estimates, of the estimate order of the same units (evaluateReport field E), the pairs on which they disagree (misorderedPairs), the claims above one half (statedAbove), the least certain claim (largestStatedError) and, for the simulated league, the wrong claims against its true values (misorderedPairs, expectedMisorderedPairs). Expected values come from v1's frozen registry (part1.json, part1-l10.json and the R case keys krw.frame.*, cde.statewide.*), the base-R oracle rows (pairCount-n, the league's misordered counts) and the postrank golden row of the six sites. Expected counts are shown with formatExpectedCount (four significant digits, corrections register CR-002) where v1 showed about three, so those expectations name the format and compare the raw value with the registry's. The prediction cases of v1 (predict-right, predict-over, predict-under, predict-skip) are gone with the gate; their numbers are the krw case's.

expect.value: ⟨count⟩ of these claims sit above one half. For independent normal posteriors, whatever their SDs, the larger posterior mean is always the more likely direction. The firms' race posteriors are not normal (KRW's prior for the race gap allows only positive values), so here it is not always (Alternative rankings from a posterior distribution and Majority comparisons and expected ranks show how such summaries part ways). The second sets this order beside majority wins: they differ on exactly these ⟨count⟩ pairs.

expect.value: The league is simulated, so its true values are known. Against them, ⟨mis⟩ of these ⟨M⟩ claims are wrong in this draw, and ⟨exp⟩ on average over new draws of the estimates. The posterior, which does not know the true values, expects ⟨E⟩. The two averages answer different questions (over new estimates for these true values; over true values, given these estimates), so they need not agree. Only this second count can be given for real units.
